# `columnConfigs`: one record per column

Part of [generated data](../generated-data.md). `emptyValueAllowed` is declared, `isFormula` is sampled, and `valueName` is declared first and sampled only as a fallback, with a summary of the columns it had to guess. Four baseline traits record each column's formula, type and head cells for `sync`.

## What is generated per column

**`columnConfigs`** (`generated/columnConfigs.ts`) — generated by `ColumnConfigOperator` (`05_Operators`) from the "Column Config" sheet, and **keyed by Table key**: the same key as the Table's entry in [`tableConfigs`](./table-configs.md), so a ticked Table's columns sit under its live Table name through `titleToName`, not under its tab's title. Only ticked Tables get Column Config rows, so only they get an entry.

**Column Config is `Table ID | Column ID | Table name | Header | Empty value allowed`, one row per column of a ticked Table, keyed by (Table ID, Column ID).** The sync appends a row for each live column ID it doesn't find, and drops a row whose Table is gone or unticked, or whose column ID is gone from its Table. The correction pass rewrites Table name from the live Table and Header from the live column. Emit resolves each row's Table ID to its Table key through this run's `tableConfigs`, and a row whose Table ID has no ticked Table Config row fails the run.

Per column, `columnId`/`valueName`/`header`/`isFormula`/`emptyValueAllowed` are generated, and so is the [baseline](#the-baseline-each-column-records) `sync` compares against; for `customDefaultValue`, see [the rules](../../src/01_SpreadsheetSchema/AGENTS.md). A column's index is not stored: `03_SpreadsheetIdentified` resolves it live from `columnId`, since a stored index would go stale as columns are added/removed/reordered.

## The baseline each column records

**Four traits record what the column looked like at the last regen**, so `sync`'s three-way comparison can tell an agent's change from a person's ([#219](https://github.com/byronbroughten/sheets-framework/issues/219)). No code compares them yet.

- **`formula`**: the top data-row cell's formula text, decompiled to brace form by `BraceFormula.decompile` against this run's configs, so `Ledger[Amount]` reads `${amount}` on Ledger and `${ledger[amount]}` elsewhere. A reference to a Table without Let api access stays as Sheets wrote it. `null` when the top cell holds no formula.
- **`columnType`**: `{ type, rule }`, the Table column's declared type (`null` for Automatic) and its data-validation `rule` as `columnProperties` carries it, `{ condition, values }`, or `null`. A dropdown's rule values stay as Sheets wrote them, braces not applied.
- **`actionRowCell`**: `null` for an empty cell, `{ kind: "checkbox" }` for any boolean, checked or not, and `{ kind: "groupHeading2", text }` for a level-2 group heading.
- **`groupHeading1`**: the level-1 group heading's text, or `null`. A heading spanning several columns is recorded on its first cell only, the one that holds the text.

**Every value comes from the run's one fetch of each Table**: `formula` from the top-row sample that sets `isFormula`, `columnType` from the `columnProperties` `valueName` already reads, and the two head cells from the action row and level-1 heading row, gathered next to the header and column ID rows.

**Each trait is optional in `makeColumnConfigs`, so a configs file written before the baseline still loads.** An absent trait is unrecorded and `null` is recorded empty, so the planner #219 specifies can take an unrecorded trait's live value as its baseline.

## `emptyValueAllowed` is declared

**`emptyValueAllowed` is *declared*** — read straight off the column's own box in Column Config (#13), which the correction pass never rewrites except on a **self-describing row**, so a tick survives a sync on a business column. A column nobody has ticked emits `false`, which is what every column emitted before, so ticking is opt-in one column at a time; don't bulk-tick formula columns, since a formula that yields a blank under some conditions and a value under others is exactly the case worth declaring individually. A newly discovered column arrives unticked, so nothing starts accepting blanks on the operator's behalf.

## `isFormula` is sampled

**`isFormula` is *sampled* — read off the described column's top data-row cell at emit time (`column.profile.isFormula`), not declared, and not stored on Column Config** — so it can flip between regenerations if someone edits that cell. Fine as data; treat it with care as a *type* axis, since a routine `gen:configs` run can then change which columns satisfy a constraint, and the resulting error surfaces far from the spreadsheet edit that caused it.

## A boolean trait keeps its literal type

A boolean trait in the generated data does keep its literal type per column, because `boolean` is a union of literal types and contextual typing doesn't widen it — that's what lets `ColumnIsFormula` resolve to `true` or `false` rather than `boolean`, and it holds for any boolean trait the config gains later.

## How `valueName` is resolved

**`valueName` is declared-first, sampled only as a fallback.**

The sync resolves it in six steps, first match winning: the ID column is always `id`; then a dropdown whose range is a **value source**, a `=<Table>[<Header>]` rule naming a column of a Let api access Table on this run, takes that source's value name, the source's generated Table key plus its header, camel-cased (`list` + `Payment status` → `listPaymentStatus`), shared by every dropdown on that source; a rule naming a Table without Let api access or an unknown header, an A1 range or a list of items falls through to the next steps and counts as untyped; then the column's own **declared column type** — the one an operator picks in the Sheets column-type menu, delivered as `columnType` on the table's `columnProperties` — maps to a primitive (`DOUBLE`/`CURRENCY`/`PERCENT` → number, `DATE` → date, `TIME`/`DATE_TIME` → **number**, `TEXT` and the chip types → string, `BOOLEAN` → **checkbox**; `DROPDOWN` and `COLUMN_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` map to nothing and fall through); then **BOOLEAN data validation** (Insert > Checkbox) on the Table column, or on the first data row if the Table did not name BOOLEAN, declares **checkbox** (`condition.type === BOOLEAN`, no values list required; other condition types are ignored here); then a **compatible number format** on the first data row maps to a primitive (`NUMBER`/`CURRENCY`/`PERCENT`/`SCIENTIFIC`/`TIME`/`DATE_TIME` → number, `DATE` → date, `TEXT` → string; omitted or `NUMBER_FORMAT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` map to nothing). Compatible means the name the sample would guess from that row equals the format's mapped name; a blank counts because that guess already consults the format. An incompatible sample stays a guess and stays untyped.

## `checkbox` comes only from a declaration

**`checkbox` is produced by declaration and by nothing else** (#12, #42) — the type menu or BOOLEAN validation, never the sample: a column that merely holds `TRUE` still produces `boolean` and stays untyped. Declaring checkbox is what buys the never-blank guarantee, so a column that samples as boolean satisfies neither the selector nor the checkbox operator, and the fix is to declare it in Sheets rather than to widen the filter. Only when nothing declares it does the old top-data-row sample decide. Every one of a checkbox column's rows draws a box, so a row nobody has touched counts as unchecked rather than as blank.

## A compatible number format is a declaration

**A compatible number format is a declaration, not a guess** (#42), including a blank first data row formatted as Currency — the type menu is never rewritten. Occupancy's "Next terms notes" read blank, undeclared and `CURRENCY`-formatted ([observed](../sheets-behaviour.md#number-formats-on-blank-cells)), and generated as a number; that column is now declared number and leaves the untyped list. A notes column that already contains text stays guessed string and untyped.

## Only a whole-day column is a `date`

**Only a whole-day column is a `date`** (#15) — a value name whose type is `SerialDate`, which a time-of-day serial would not satisfy, so the datetime formats map to plain numbers until there is a datetime value name to give them.

## The untyped-columns summary

Because a column left on Automatic with no mapped format and no Insert > Checkbox declares nothing, the sample is still doing real work: **the sync counts every column whose value name it had to guess and returns a one-line summary**, naming how many Tables they span, which the config-sync endpoint writes into its run status cell; the per-Table breakdown goes to the execution log. The sync never fails over an untyped column — it also writes missing column IDs and appends Column Config rows, and a throw would discard all of that. **That run status cell is written by the endpoint, not by the sync.** `npm run gen:configs` calls `ConfigCoordinator` on the Node host, so it writes no start time and no run status — to see the summary on the sheet, tick the sync endpoint's checkbox instead. On the command line the summary rides back with the three file sources (`ConfigRegeneration.untypedColumnsSummary`) and the script prints it, because a command line has no cell to write into and the only signal the sync produces would otherwise be lost; the per-Table breakdown still goes to the log. **The agent must report that count**, per `gen:configs`' standing permission in the byro-repo root's `docs/targets-and-gates.md`.

## The generated entry never says which step decided it

**The generated entry itself never says which step decided it.** A declared `CURRENCY` column type and a `CURRENCY` number format under a blank top cell both emit `valueName: "number"`, so a wrong value name in `columnConfigs.ts` doesn't tell you whether to change a declaration or add one. That summary is the only signal the app gives; from outside it, read the live declared types directly (see [`docs/how-it-runs/gworkspace-mcp.md`](../how-it-runs/gworkspace-mcp.md)).
